metadata.content: Newmarket: Musical Times stays unbeaten with Fillies' Mile victory for Charlie Appleby with William Buick on board | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Newmarket: Musical Times stays unbeaten with Fillies' Mile victory for Charlie Appleby with William Buick on board Musical Times confirmed her Classic prospects with a dramatic success in the Group One Fillies' Mile at Newmarket, overcoming a host of traffic problems to land her first success at the top level Friday 9 October 2026 16:36, UK Image: Musical Times, ridden by William Buick, on the way to winning the bet365 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket Musical Times overcame traffic problems to maintain her unbeaten record in the bet365 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket. Charlie Appleby's youngster had looked a top-class prospect in winning her first two starts on the July Course and at Yarmouth, and completed her hat-trick with facile victory in the May Hill Stakes at Doncaster last month. Subsequent 1000 Guineas heroine Desert Flower completed the May Hill-Fillies' Mile double two years ago for Appleby and William Buick and Musical Times was the 4/9 favourite to follow suit. It was not entirely straightforward for odds-on backers, with Buick struggling to find a gap, but once the split did come she quickly went through the gears to beat Aidan O'Brien's Haven by a length. messages.text: Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades

metadata.summary: World Championship leader Kimi Antonelli cast further doubt over the performance of Mercedes' recent upgrade package as he explained his car was "very difficult" to drive during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore.
metadata.content: Singapore GP: Kimi Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades after disappointing Sprint Qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Singapore GP: Kimi Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades after disappointing Sprint Qualifying Kimi Antonelli says his upgraded Mercedes is "very unpredictable" after only qualifying seventh for the Singapore GP Sprint; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Friday 9 October 2026 17:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell and Kimi Antonelli discuss Mercedes' new upgrade package World Championship leader Kimi Antonelli cast further doubt over the performance of Mercedes' recent upgrade package as he explained his car was "very difficult" to drive during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore. After the long-awaited upgrades failed to deliver improved performance when they debuted at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Mercedes decided to compare different specifications of the car in Singapore. Antonelli is running the latest version, which included an additional front wing that had not been available in Malaysia, while George Russell is running the pre-Malaysia version of the car that he won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in last month. messages.text: FIA admits 'human error' created power disparity in Singapore Sprint Qualifying

metadata.summary: The FIA has admitted "human error" caused a power disparity during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore.
metadata.content: Singapore GP: FIA admits 'human error' created power disparity in Sprint Qualifying at Marina Bay Street Circuit | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Singapore GP: FIA admits 'human error' created power disparity in Sprint Qualifying at Marina Bay Street Circuit Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, has revealed a "human error" caused a power disparity in the first part of Sprint Qualifying on Friday; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 9 October 2026 16:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Craig Slater explains the FIA 'human error' which cause a power disparity between the car during Sprint qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix The FIA has admitted "human error" caused a power disparity during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore. Following a red flag for debris in SQ1 caused by Cadillac's Sergio Perez, the FIA did not activate Overtake Mode - an extra power boost that is normally active throughout qualifying and used in races to aid overtaking. The FIA reactivated Overtake Mode for 27 seconds before deactivating it again, thus causing an unfair advantage in the first part of Sprint Qualifying. metadata.content: David Moyes: Everton manager admits surprise at seeing the club being put up for sale by The Friedkin Group | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content David Moyes: Everton manager admits surprise at seeing the club being put up for sale by The Friedkin Group Everton were put up for sale again on Friday; owners The Friedkin Group (TFG) have said they will only entertain interest from parties who they feel are the "right stewards to take the club forward"; TFG only completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024 Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Friday 9 October 2026 18:13, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Everton manager David Moyes says he was surprised to hear that the club's owners were keen to sell the club after less than two years in charge David Moyes has admitted his surprise at Everton being put up for sale by owners The Friedkin Group - even claiming he only found out on Friday morning when the statement was released to the supporters. The Friedkin Group (TFG) announced they are open to new investment into the club - including the "potential sale of a controlling interest". The group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin , only completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024 - ending Farhad Moshiri's long spell at the helm. messages.text: Verstappen keeps Singapore Sprint pole after investigation

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen maintained his rich vein of form to claim pole position for Saturday's Sprint at the Singapore Grand Prix, which he kept after avoiding a penalty in an investigation over yellow flags.
metadata.content: Singapore GP Sprint Qualifying: Max Verstappen keeps pole position from George Russell after avoiding yellow flags penalty | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update Singapore GP Sprint Qualifying: Max Verstappen keeps pole position from George Russell after avoiding yellow flags penalty Red Bull's Max Verstappen tops Sprint Qualifying and avoids yellow flags penalty after investigation; George Russell second, Kimi Antonelli only seventh; watch the Singapore Sprint on Saturday at 10am (build-up from 9am) ahead of Qualifying at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Friday 9 October 2026 17:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Qualifying for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix Sprint race. Max Verstappen maintained his rich vein of form to claim pole position for Saturday's Sprint at the Singapore Grand Prix, which he kept after avoiding a penalty in an investigation over yellow flags. Fresh from finally winning Red Bull's first race of the season from their first pole last week in Malaysia, Verstappen needed just a single flying lap at the end of SQ3 to claim pole by just over a tenth of a second from Mercedes' George Russell. But championship leader Kimi Antonelli was only seventh in the other Mercedes, the one featuring their problematic upgrade introduced last week in Malaysia.
